passage: When Liam's email arrived, Tariq was eating toast over the sink in their Manchester flat: My first solo exhibition! Opening Friday. Tariq read it twice. Something sour rose in his chest, and a sentence formed on its own: It's only a café wall, really. He put the phone down. Okay, he thought. That's envy. He and Liam had started painting at the same evening class. Tariq had stopped after six months, busy with overtime. He picked the phone up again and wrote: Mate, that's brilliant. I'll be there Friday. Proud of you. Then, after a moment: Can I buy you a coffee after and hear how you found the time? He sent it, and pulled out the box under his bed where his paints still were.

qa.q: Where was Tariq when Liam's email arrived?
qa.a: Eating toast over the sink in the Manchester flat.

qa.q: What did Tariq realise when the sentence "It's only a café wall, really" formed?
qa.a: Tariq recognised that thought as envy, not a fair judgment of Liam's achievement. 🤔

qa.q: What turning point does Tariq reach at the end, and what might it lead to?
qa.a: Asking how Liam found the time and pulling out the paints shows Tariq turning envy into a question about personal goals, which might lead back to painting.

qa.q: How might Liam feel reading Tariq's reply?
qa.a: Liam would likely feel supported by a friend from the old evening class, and pleased that Tariq wants to hear more.

grounding: An adult notices his envy at a friend's exhibition, congratulates the friend, and asks what it shows about his own goals.

passage: The team huddle ended with the announcement: Chetan would lead the new payments project. People clapped. Saurabh clapped a beat late. Walking back to his desk, he caught himself drafting a message to a friend: Chetan's good at presentations, that's all. He deleted it. He'd wanted that project; he'd said so in his last review. He sat with the feeling for a minute. Envy. Fine. What was it telling him? That he wanted to lead, and hadn't volunteered for anything visible all year. He walked over to Chetan's desk. "Congratulations. Genuinely. Can I ask what you did to get it?" Chetan blinked, then grinned. "Coffee? I'll tell you what I'd do if I were you."

qa.q: Which project would Chetan lead?
qa.a: The new payments project.

qa.q: What do Saurabh's late clap and deleted message suggest about Saurabh's feelings?
qa.a: They suggest a sting of envy that Saurabh noticed and chose not to act on.

qa.q: How did naming the envy change Saurabh's next move?
qa.a: Naming it showed Saurabh a real wish to lead, so instead of undermining Chetan, Saurabh congratulated Chetan and asked for advice.

qa.q: How might Chetan experience Saurabh's question?
qa.a: Chetan might feel pleasantly surprised and respected, and glad to help a colleague who also wanted the project.

grounding: A professional names his envy at a colleague's new role, congratulates the colleague and asks what it shows about his own goals.

passage:
Dear Akash,
I owe you a proper note, not just the thumbs-up I sent in the group.
When you told us your short story was accepted by the literary magazine, my first feeling wasn't joy. It was a pinch. We started writing together in college, and I've had eleven rejections this year. For a day I caught myself thinking your ending was rushed. It wasn't. It's beautiful.
So: congratulations. Really. I'm proud to know you.
And the pinch told me something useful. I've been writing less and complaining more. I want what you have, so I'm going to write every morning this month.
Would you read my next draft, when it's ready?
Aparna

qa.q: How many rejections has Aparna had this year?
qa.a: Eleven rejections.

qa.q: What was Aparna's first feeling about Akash's news, and why?
qa.a: A pinch of envy rather than joy, because they started writing together and Aparna has had many rejections.

qa.q: What choice did Aparna make with that pinch of envy?
qa.a: Aparna named it, congratulated Akash properly, and used it as a sign to write every morning this month.

qa.q: What might this honest note mean to Akash?
qa.a: Akash may feel moved by the honesty and trusted, and glad the success is celebrated rather than resented. ❤️

grounding: A young adult owns envy at a fellow writer's publication, congratulates them, and turns it into a personal writing goal.

passage: You want the honest version, Vaibhav? Okay. Last March, my junior from B.Ed college, Rukhsar, won the state award for young teachers. Two years younger than me. When I saw the photo, my first thought was: she only won because her school is in the city. I actually typed half of that to a friend. Then I stopped and said it out loud in my empty kitchen: Yamini, you're jealous. Just call it what it is. It felt silly, but it helped. So I deleted the message and called Rukhsar instead. I said congratulations and I meant most of it. Then I asked what she'd done in her classroom that got noticed. She laughed, said "Thank you, Didi," and told me about her reading corner for first-generation learners. And I realised the award didn't sting because of her. It stung because I've wanted to start something like that for three years and haven't.

qa.q: What award did Rukhsar win?
qa.a: She won the state award for young teachers.

qa.q: What did Yamini realise the sting was really about?
qa.a: She realised it stung because she had wanted to start something similar for three years and hadn't.

qa.q: Which choice turned Yamini's envy into something useful?
qa.a: Naming the jealousy aloud, deleting the message and calling Rukhsar to ask what she did let Yamini learn from her instead of undermining her.

qa.q: What would have changed if Yamini had sent the half-typed message?
qa.a: The friend might have repeated the dig, Rukhsar could have been hurt, and Yamini would have missed what the award showed about her own goals.

grounding: An adult names her envy, congratulates the achiever and asks what the success reveals about her own goals.

passage: I'm Chinmay, and I work the grill next to Thomas at a restaurant kitchen in Kochi. Last month Chef announced that Ruth would be the new sous-chef. Ruth joined after Thomas. The kitchen went quiet in that way kitchens never do. Thomas put his tongs down and said, not loudly, "Honestly? I'm jealous. Give me a minute." Then he walked out to the back step. When he came back, he went straight to Ruth, shook her hand and said, "You earned that. How did you prepare for the tasting?" She told him about practising the sauces every night for weeks. The next morning I saw him asking Chef what he'd need to work on to be considered next time. I don't know what went through his head on that back step. But he's been coming in an hour early since.

qa.q: Where does Chinmay work alongside Thomas?
qa.a: At the grill of a restaurant kitchen in Kochi.

qa.q: What does Thomas's saying "I'm jealous. Give me a minute" suggest about him?
qa.a: It suggests he noticed his envy and chose to name it honestly instead of letting it come out as a dig at Ruth.

qa.q: Why was Thomas's question to Chef the next morning a turning point?
qa.a: It turned his envy into a clear goal, finding out what he needed to improve to be considered next time.

qa.q: How might Ruth feel when Thomas shakes her hand and asks about her preparation?
qa.a: Ruth might feel relieved and respected, especially after the tense silence, since a senior colleague is backing her.

grounding: A colleague watches an adult name his envy, congratulate the promoted peer and ask what it means for his own goals.
